clue.text: Having packed, finally decides to get married

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word decides

parts.note: last letter of decides
to wed is to get married

explanation.surface: Someone, bags already packed, at last makes up their mind to tie the knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowed means put away or packed, so having stowed things is having packed them.

clue.text: My first drink supplier leaves on time

definitions.note: a baby's first drink, milk, comes from this

parts.note: tea is made from leaves, so leaves can stand for tea

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the person who supplied their first drink leaving promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places TEA before T in the across-reading sense of a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A nipple supplies milk, the first drink any infant takes, so it is a witty description of the source.

clue.text: Sack producer Marie knew to be dissipated

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered or dissolute, so the letters of Marie knew are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Marie realised some producer of sacks was living a dissolute life.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack here is the old name for a dry white wine from Spain, as drunk by Falstaff, not a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Sack is a fortified white wine, so a vintner who makes it is a producer of sack.

clue.text: Thin cover lifted on truck

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word is raised up, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a cover
ute, short for utility vehicle, is an Australian word for a pickup truck

explanation.surface: A thin cover is hoisted onto a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: To thin a liquid is to water it down, the verb sense of making weaker.

clue.text: Old diary found in one busy Yankee vintner's study

indicators.note: found in says the diary word sits inside the letters that follow
busy suggests activity and bustle, so the letters of one are stirred into a new order

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a log is a diary or record

explanation.surface: An old diary turns up belonging to an energetic American wine merchant.
explanation.walkthrough: Vintner's study reads like a room in a wine merchant's house; it is the field of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oenology is the science and study of wine and winemaking, the vintner's field.

clue.text: Nine under the table

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally the number that is one more than eight
second meaning: drunk, having had one drink too many

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being slightly drunk is read literally as arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means tipsy, a drink beyond one's limit; read literally, one over eight is nine.

clue.text: Last snifter near Deal, heading north

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the word is read upwards, from the end back

parts.note: a pact is a deal or agreement

explanation.surface: A final brandy close to the town of Deal, before travelling north.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal looks like the Kent seaside town; it is the noun meaning agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is the drink taken just before bed, the final tipple of the evening.

clue.text: Fast over played slowly

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
O is the cricket scoreboard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Something fast is played slowly, a paradox of tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast seems the opposite of the definition; it is the noun for a period of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the Italian musical direction telling performers to play at a slow tempo.

clue.text: Barrel seen in depot about new place for empties

indicators.note: seen in places the barrel letter inside the depot word

parts.note: a garage is a depot for vehicles, as for buses
b is an abbreviation for barrel as a unit of measure
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A barrel is spotted in a depot near a new spot for empty bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: Empties sound like returnable bottles at a pub; the place is an American rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A garbage can is the US term for a rubbish bin, where empty containers are thrown away.

clue.text: Scot isn't able to cover first two of Ullapool drains

indicators.note: to cover means to go around, so the Scottish word wraps the other letters

parts.note: cannae is Scots for cannot

indicators.note: first two of takes only the opening pair of letters from the following word

parts.note: first two letters of Ullapool

explanation.surface: A Scot cannot cover the drains of the first part of Ullapool, a Highland port.
explanation.walkthrough: Ullapool is a fishing village in the Scottish Highlands, fitting the Scots word cannae.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannulae are thin tubes inserted into the body, used for example to drain fluid in surgery.

clue.text: Information on tax swells

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
to try someone is to tax or strain them, as in trying their patience

explanation.surface: Details about tax rises, as in tax bills that swell.
explanation.walkthrough: Swells looks like a verb about growing; it is the noun for fashionable upper-class people.
explanation.definitionFit: Swells is old slang for smart, well-to-do people, the landed classes.

clue.text: Driving test on one tank on island with learner

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for UK vehicles
I is the Roman numeral for one
a vat is a large tank
Iona is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A driving test taken in a tank on an island, with a learner at the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about cars, but driving is the adjective meaning inspiring or pushing forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motivational is driving in the sense of providing the impetus that spurs people on.

clue.text: Estonia's perplexed with old barren state

indicators.note: perplexed means confused, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: Estonia, with the 's read as is, a link

explanation.surface: Estonia is baffled by an old, unfruitful nation.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a country, matching Estonia, but it means a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolation is a bleak, empty condition, a wasteland where nothing grows.

clue.text: Pet swallow

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to kiss and cuddle, as courting couples do
second meaning: to drink quickly, gulp down

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are informal British verbs: to canoodle, and to down a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Necking is kissing and caressing; to neck a pint is to gulp it down fast.

clue.text: Sibyl's about to down a litre twice — of these?

definitions.text: Sibyl's about to down a litre twice — of these?

indicators.note: to down is to swallow, so the litres go inside the prophet word
about turns the prophet word round, reading it from the end

parts.note: a sibyl is a prophetess or seer; the 's is is

indicators.note: twice says the pair of letters just given is written a second time

explanation.surface: A prophetess is about to knock back two litres of some drink, and the clue asks which.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a seer gulping litres of beer invites the question of what drink, and the answer is cask-conditioned British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is traditional cask-conditioned beer, the kind a seer might quaff by the litre.

clue.text: Not everyone stands up in a church together

indicators.note: in places the reversed phrase inside the letters A and CE

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

indicators.note: in a down clue, stands up means the phrase is read upwards

parts.note: not everyone means not all

explanation.surface: Some, but not all, of a congregation get to their feet in church at once.
explanation.definitionFit: All at once means simultaneously, everyone at the same moment, so together.

clue.text: Plastered husband before noon has me blushing

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon
red describes a blushing face

explanation.surface: A husband drunk before midday makes the speaker blush.
explanation.walkthrough: Plastered might suggest wall rendering; here it is slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammered and plastered are both slang words meaning extremely drunk.

clue.text: Our mum's spiking another mum's whiskey

indicators.note: spiking means piercing, so the first pair of words goes into the other mum word

parts.note: mum as in keep mum means be quiet, so sh
taken as written
mum is ma, and the possessive keeps its S

explanation.surface: One mother is lacing another mother's whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: The second mum is not a mother but the word for silence, as in keep mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour mash is a whiskey made using some old mash to start fermentation, typical of bourbon.

clue.text: Disclose what boozer often needs?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to reveal secret information
second meaning: a heavy drinker often needs to urinate

explanation.walkthrough: A boozer can be a pub or a drinker; either way the slang take a leak fits.
explanation.definitionFit: To leak is to divulge secrets; a leak is also slang for urination, which beer prompts.

clue.text: Mixed drink, say, going off without one

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order
without says a letter is left out of the fodder before it is rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cocktail, for example, is spoiling without one ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: Mixed looks like part of the definition's description, but the drink is defined by the whole phrase and 'off' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a mixed drink of eggs, milk, sugar and often spirits, a Christmas favourite.

clue.text: One fights egg producer with rowing team

parts.note: a bantam is a small hen, which lays eggs
an eight is a racing crew of eight rowers

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a hen and a crew of rowers in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantamweight is a boxer in a light weight class, someone who fights for sport.

clue.text: Taste too much? That's out of order

indicators.note: out of means taken out of, so the order letters are removed from too much

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Drinking too much is judged unacceptable behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: That's out of order sounds like a rebuke; 'That's' links, and OM leaves too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch is a small amount or trace, as is a taste: a touch of brandy.

clue.text: The Italian's stopping doctor's tipple

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the Italian article goes into the doctor letters

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine
il is the Italian for the; the 's is is

explanation.surface: An Italian man is preventing his doctor from having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild is a dark, lightly hopped British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild is a style of beer, a tipple drunk in British pubs.

clue.text: Caught one using tongue to taste spirit

indicators.note: caught is used for heard, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a licker uses the tongue to taste

explanation.surface: Someone is caught licking a spirit to sample it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is distilled alcoholic drink, the spirits such as whisky or gin.

clue.text: Cocktail Indian spilt in fast car

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the car letters

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, a fast touring car

indicators.note: spilt suggests letters scattered by accident

explanation.surface: A cocktail spilt by an Indian in a sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and It is gin mixed with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin and It is a classic mixed drink of gin and sweet vermouth, a cocktail.

clue.text: Train hooted, skirting theatre punctually

indicators.note: skirting means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the theatre letters
to train is to direct or shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: NT is the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: A train sounded its horn passing round a theatre, exactly on time.
explanation.walkthrough: Train looks like the railway noun; it is a verb meaning to shape, so it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: On the dot means exactly at the appointed time, so punctually.

clue.text: Ravenous guy, empty, wolfs venison that's turned

indicators.note: wolfs means eats greedily, so the man's outer letters swallow the venison word
empty means hollowed out, leaving only the first and last letters
turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: venison is the meat of deer

explanation.surface: A starving man devours some venison that has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy means wanting food intensely, a voracious, hungry appetite.
